facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
no breast symptoms
a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast
no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding
a tomosynthesis-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the right inner breast was performed
yielding 12 core specimens
marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils
with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata
no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis
Peripheral blood eosinophil levels were within the normal range
Hypereosinophilic syndrome was excluded from consideration
asymptomatic

The patient has a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast, which could be consistent with a benign breast lesion.
The patient has peripheral blood eosinophil levels within the normal range, but has a history of eosinophilic infiltration, which could be consistent with idiopathic eosinophilia.
The patient is asymptomatic and has no breast symptoms, which is consistent with an asymptomatic breast condition.

rationales.F03: The new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast is a significant finding that increases the likelihood of chronic inflammatory breast disease, fibrocystic change, and benign breast lesion.
rationales.F07: The presence of marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils is highly suggestive of chronic inflammatory breast disease and eosinophilic mastitis.
rationales.F11: The exclusion of hypereosinophilic syndrome from consideration decreases the likelihood of idiopathic eosinophilia.
